heading: 3-Day Suzhou Itinerary for First-Time Visitors (2026)

byline.name: Maintained by Lin
byline.tested: Prices, hours and booking rules checked against official sources, October 2026

items: **Day 1:** the Humble Administrator's Garden at opening time, Suzhou Museum a short walk away, then Pingjiang Road.
**Day 2:** the Lingering Garden and the western old city.
**Day 3:** Tiger Hill, a smaller garden, or a whole day in a water town.

quickAnswer: Book ahead with your passport: the Humble Administrator's Garden (¥70–80) and the Lingering Garden (¥45–55) take real-name bookings, and Suzhou Museum is free but needs a reserved slot and is closed on Mondays. Stay in or near the old city.

blocks.text: **How to book the gardens.** The Humble Administrator's Garden, the Lingering Garden and the Lion Grove Garden take real-name bookings. Book them on the official WeChat account **苏州园林旅游** (Suzhou Gardens Tourism), using your passport. In 2024, Suzhou said it had also put the tickets on Trip.com. Most of the other gardens the city runs dropped real-name booking in 2024, so you can scan the code at the gate and pay. Big holidays can sell out: Xinhua reported the Humble Administrator's Garden was fully booked over the 2025 May Day holiday.

**Suzhou Museum.** The main building, a short walk from the Humble Administrator's Garden, is free, but you need a timed slot. Slots open 7 days ahead at 8:00 on the museum's website, its WeChat account **苏州博物馆**, or the mini program **苏州博物馆全预约**. Bring the passport you booked with, and arrive within 30 minutes of your slot. **Suzhou Museum West**, at 399 Changjiang Road outside the old city, is a separate branch that doesn't need a booking. Make sure you're going to the right one.
**Paying.** In 2024, Suzhou said its major sights had card machines for foreign bank cards. For everyday payments, see the [China payment guide](/china-payment-guide/).

sections.title: Day 1: gardens, museum and Pingjiang Road

items: Take the first slot at the **Humble Administrator's Garden**, 178 Dongbei Street. It opens at 7:30; arrive between 7:30 and 9:00 to avoid the crowds. Take Metro Line 6 to Zhuozhengyuan Subo station, Exit 2, about a 5–10 minute walk. In summer 2026 it opened at 6:45 for the lotus season (June 19–October 7), so check the hours if you visit in summer.
Walk to **Suzhou Museum** for your reserved slot. It's free, opens at 9:00 and is closed on Mondays.
Walk **Pingjiang Road** slowly, turning into side lanes and crossing the small bridges instead of treating it as one photo stop.
Have dinner near the old city or your hotel. If it rains, spend longer in the museum instead of walking the canals.

sections.title: Day 2: Lingering Garden and the western old city

items: Visit the **Lingering Garden**, 338 Liuyuan Road, for its halls, courtyards, rockwork and framed views. It opens at 7:30 and takes real-name bookings like the Humble Administrator's Garden.
Add one stop that matches your interests: a smaller garden, a craft venue, or a walk along Shantang Street.
Take a food break instead of crossing town for several more gardens. Try a Suzhou noodle shop, and confirm the ingredients if you have allergies.
In the evening, walk by the canals, or check whether the **Master of the Nets Garden** night garden is running. It's ¥120 on the official price list, and in 2025 it ran from March 7 to November 16.

items: Choose one complete third-day route. A water town plus several central gardens is too much for most first-time visitors.
If you have an afternoon train, keep the last stop close to the station and collect your luggage before the rush.

sections.title: Where to stay and how to arrive from Shanghai

items: For two garden-heavy days, stay near the old city or a metro stop close to your hotel. A hotel beside a distant railway station can cost you sightseeing time.
Suzhou, Suzhou North and Suzhou Industrial Park are different railway stations, and Shanghai has several major stations too. Read the exact stations on your ticket.
Book on 12306 or Trip.com with the passport you'll travel on. Tickets go on sale 15 days before departure. [How to book China trains](/china-train-travel-guide/)
Before you book a hotel, check its "Guests Accepted" line on Trip.com ([how](/china-hotels-for-foreigners/#check-before-booking)), and save its Chinese name, address and phone number.
A day trip from Shanghai can cover one garden and a nearby neighbourhood. Three days let you see Suzhou's gardens, canals and food at a slower pace.
[3-day Nanjing itinerary](/3-day-nanjing-itinerary/): Sun Yat-sen Mausoleum, Nanjing Museum, the Qinhuai River, city walls and train tips.

items: In summer, start early and keep shade, water and an indoor break in the plan. In rain, stone paths and bridges get slippery.
The prices and hours on this page come from official sources, checked in October 2026. They can change on holidays, so check again shortly before you go.
**One day:** the Humble Administrator's Garden plus Pingjiang Road, adding Suzhou Museum if you've booked a slot (not on a Monday).
**Two days:** keep the northeast cluster and the Lingering Garden on separate days; save the water town for another trip.
**With children or limited mobility:** one major garden a day, shorter lane walks, and check step-free routes and taxi drop-off points.
**Garden lovers:** replace Day 3's excursion with smaller gardens that differ in size and design. If you prefer canals and street life, visit fewer gardens.

faqs.question: Are three days enough for Suzhou?
faqs.answer: Yes. Three full days let you explore the northeast old city, the Lingering Garden area and one flexible third-day route without rushing. Count arrival and departure time separately.

faqs.question: Can Suzhou be a day trip from Shanghai?
faqs.answer: Yes for one garden and a nearby neighbourhood, provided you confirm the exact stations and train times. Stay overnight to see more gardens, food and canals at a slower pace.

faqs.question: Which Suzhou railway station should I use?
faqs.answer: Use the station printed on your ticket. Suzhou, Suzhou North and Suzhou Industrial Park are separate stations with different hotel and old-city transfers.

faqs.question: Do I need to reserve Suzhou Museum and gardens?
faqs.answer: Yes, for the big ones. The Humble Administrator's Garden, the Lingering Garden and the Lion Grove Garden take real-name bookings on the official WeChat account 苏州园林旅游; foreign visitors book with a passport, and the Humble Administrator's Garden sells no tickets on site. Suzhou Museum's main building is free, but slots open 7 days ahead at 8:00, and it's closed on Mondays except public holidays.

faqs.question: Should I add Tongli to a three-day Suzhou itinerary?
faqs.answer: It can fill one whole day if canals and a water town matter more than additional city gardens. Confirm transport in both directions and avoid stacking another distant town.

faqs.question: Can ChinaEase Buddy personalise this Suzhou plan?
faqs.answer: Yes. Share your Shanghai connection, dates, hotel area, garden and museum interests, walking pace and onward station for a practical three-day route.

faqs.question: How much are Suzhou garden tickets?
faqs.answer: On the Suzhou Gardens Bureau's price list, the Humble Administrator's Garden is ¥80 in April, May and July–October and ¥70 the rest of the year. The Lingering Garden is ¥55 / ¥45, Tiger Hill ¥70 / ¥60, and the Lion Grove and Master of the Nets gardens ¥40 / ¥30. Suzhou Museum is free.
